notes.urn:cts:greekLit:tlg1118.tlg003.1st1K-gr: hierakites (“hawk-stone”) is not securely identified, nor is the Diogenes who wrote On Stones.

nodes.text: The hierakites stone and the Indian stone, tied onto the right thigh, dry up haemorrhoids, as we too have found by trial. And Diogenes, in his [work] On Stones, says this: “The hierakites stone is greenish and verges on black; and it has the power of drying up haemorrhoids.”
